content: If any one compliments him, he laughs to himself at the person who compliments him; and if any one censures him, he makes no defense.
author: Epictetus
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Epictetus understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
